'''Philip Joseph Kocienski''' {{post-nominals|size=100%|country=GBR|FRS}} (born 23 December 1946<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Członkowie Polskiej Akademii Nauk|url=http://czlonkowie.pan.pl/czlonkowie/sites/WynikiWyszukiwania.html?s=KOCIE%C5%83SKI,+Philip|access-date=2021-04-30|website=czlonkowie.pan.pl}}</ref>) is a British [[organic chemistry|organic chemist]]. He is an Emeritus Professor at the [[University of Leeds]].<ref>[http://www.chem.leeds.ac.uk/index.php?id=163&person=61 Alphabetical staff list] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160314012650/http://www.chem.leeds.ac.uk/index.php?id=163&person=61 |date=14 March 2016 }}, University of Leeds. Retrieved 13 March 2016.</ref>

== Research ==
Kocienski has made contributions to the design and development of new [[organometallic]] [[reagent]]s in [[Chemical synthesis|synthesis]], and the applications of synthetic methods to complex natural products. Early work with [[Basil Lythgoe]] on the scope and [[stereochemistry]] of the [[Julia olefination]] with alpha-metallated [[sulphone]] reagents emphasised the value of this method in organic chemistry. His major contribution has been to research the synthesis and chemistry of novel [[metalation|metallated]] (lithium, copper and nickel) [[enol ether]]s, and to develop the uses of these intermediates in the synthesis of oxacyclic and geometrically defined [[alkene]] units in natural products of biological significance. Kocienski has synthesised the [[insecticide]] milbemycin beta 3, the [[potassium channel blocker]] talaromycin B, the [[hypotension|hypotensive]] agent lacrimin, and the [[antihypertensive agent]] zoapatanol. His [[total synthesis]] of the insect toxin [[pederin]], and his synthetic work toward the [[immunosuppressant]] [[Tacrolimus|FK 506]], have made him regarded as one of the leading organic chemists in the field.<ref name="FRS" />

== Awards and honours ==
In 1984 Kocienski received the [[Hickinbottom Award|Hickinbottom Fellowship]] of the Royal Society of Chemistry.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.rsc.org/ScienceAndTechnology/Awards/HickinbottomAward/PreviousWinners.asp|title=Hickinbottom Award Previous Winners |publisher= Royal Society of Chemistry|accessdate = 1 May 2016}}</ref> He was elected a [[List of Fellows of the Royal Society elected in 1997|Fellow of the Royal Society (FRS) in 1997]].<ref name="FRS">{{cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/philip-kocienski-11765|title=Philip Kocienski|publisher=[[Royal Society]]|location=London}} One or more of the preceding sentences may incorporate text from the royalsociety.org website where "all text published under the heading 'Biography' on Fellow profile pages is available under [[Creative Commons license|Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License]]." {{cite web |url=https://royalsociety.org/about-us/terms-conditions-policies/ |title=Royal Society Terms, conditions and policies |accessdate=9 March 2016 |url-status=bot: unknown |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160220093712/https://royalsociety.org/about-us/terms-conditions-policies/ |archivedate=20 February 2016 }}</ref> He won the [[Marie Curie Medal]] in 1997. Since 2000 he has been a foreign member of [[Polish Academy of Sciences]].<ref name=":0" />
